questions.question_text:
A loan of $\$22\,000$ is taken at $9\%$ p.a. over $3$ years ($36$ months).
Using the repayment table value of $\$31.80$ per $\$1000$ borrowed, calculate the monthly repayment.

options.why: Multiplied table value by $2.2$ instead of $22$ ($22\,000 / 1000$).
Divided the principal by $100$ instead of $1000$, then calculated $31.80 \times 220 = \$6996.00$.
Used the $60$-month rate of $\$20.76$ instead of the $36$-month rate.
Read the $12$-month column ($\$88.85$) without converting $2$ years into $24$ months.
Used the $36$-month rate ($\$33.21$) for $3$ years instead of $2$ years.
Used the $8\%$ interest rate table value ($\$45.23$) instead of the $12\%$ value.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Term in months} = 2 \times 12 = 24$
$\text{Table rate (}12\%\text{ p.a., } 24\text{ months)} = \$47.07$
$\text{Monthly repayment} = 47.07 \times \frac{\$16\,000}{1000}$
$= 47.07 \times 16$
$= \$753.12$

questions.question_text:
A $\$18\,000$ loan at $8\%$ p.a. over $4$ years ($48$ months) has a monthly repayment rate of $\$24.41$ per $\$1000$ borrowed.
Calculate the total interest paid over the term of the loan.

options.why: Gave the total amount repaid instead of the total interest paid.
Multiplied the monthly repayment by $4$ years instead of $48$ months, calculating $\$439.38 \times 4 - \$18\,000 = -\$16\,242.48$.
Used the $5$-year rate and term, calculating $20.28 \times 18 \times 60 - 18\,000 = \$3902.40$.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the monthly repayment**
$\text{Monthly} = 24.41 \times 18 = \$439.38$
2. **Calculate the total amount repaid**
$\text{Total repaid} = 48 \times \$439.38 = \$21\,090.24$
3. **Calculate the total interest**
$\text{Interest} = \$21\,090.24 - \$18\,000$
$= \$3090.24$

questions.question_text:
A borrower takes a $\$25\,000$ loan at $11\%$ p.a. over $5$ years ($60$ months), where the table rate is $\$21.74$ per $\$1000$.
What is the total amount repaid on the loan?

options.why: Calculated only the total interest paid instead of the total amount repaid.
Multiplied monthly repayment by $50$ months instead of $60$ months.
Assumed a flat total interest charge of $40\%$ of the principal, calculating $\$25\,000 + 0.40 \times \$25\,000 = \$35\,000$ instead of using the repayments.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the monthly repayment**
$\text{Monthly repayment} = 21.74 \times 25 = \$543.50$
2. **Calculate the total amount repaid**
$\text{Total repaid} = 60 \times \$543.50$
$= \$32\,610.00$

questions.question_text:
A $\$21\,000$ loan at $10\%$ p.a. is repaid over $5$ years ($60$ months).
The table rate is $\$21.25$ per $\$1000$ borrowed.
Calculate the total interest paid.

options.why: Gave the total repayments, $\$446.25 \times 60 = \$26\,775$, without subtracting the principal.
Gave only the monthly repayment, $21.25 \times 21 = \$446.25$.
Used $36$ repayments instead of $60$, calculating $\$446.25 \times 36 - \$21\,000 = -\$4935$.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the monthly repayment**
$\text{Monthly repayment} = 21.25 \times 21 = \$446.25$
2. **Calculate the total amount repaid**
$\text{Total repaid} = 60 \times \$446.25 = \$26\,775.00$
3. **Calculate the total interest**
$\text{Interest} = \$26\,775.00 - \$21\,000 = \$5775.00$

questions.question_text:
A borrower takes a $\$27\,000$ loan at $11\%$ p.a. over $4$ years ($48$ months).
The table rate is $\$25.85$ per $\$1000$ borrowed.
Calculate the monthly repayment.

options.why: Gave the repayment for only $\$1000$ borrowed without multiplying by $27$.
Divided the principal by $10\,000$ instead of $1000$, calculating $25.85 \times 2.7 = \$69.795 \approx \$69.80$.
Used the $36$-month rate, calculating $32.74 \times 27 = \$883.98$.

questions.question_text:
A $\$17\,500$ loan is taken at $14\%$ p.a. over $4$ years ($48$ months).
The table rate is $\$27.33$ per $\$1000$ borrowed.
Calculate the monthly repayment to the nearest cent.

options.why: Used the $8\%$ rate, calculating $24.41 \times 17.5 = \$427.175 \approx \$427.18$.
Divided the principal by $10\,000$ instead of $1000$, calculating $27.33 \times 1.75 = \$47.8275 \approx \$47.83$.
Divided the principal by $100$ instead of $1000$, calculating $27.33 \times 175 = \$4782.75$.

questions.question_text:
Daniel borrows $\$34\,600$ at $8\%$ p.a. over $5$ years ($60$ months).
The table rate is $\$20.28$ per $\$1000$ borrowed.
Calculate the total interest paid. Round the monthly repayment to the nearest cent and use those rounded payments in the total.

options.why: Used the unrounded monthly amount, calculating $\$701.688 \times 60 - \$34\,600 = \$7501.28$ instead of using cent-rounded payments.
Gave total repayments, $\$701.69 \times 60 = \$42\,101.40$, without subtracting the principal.
Gave the rounded monthly repayment instead of calculating the total interest.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the monthly repayment**
$\text{Monthly repayment} = 20.28 \times 34.6 = \$701.688 \approx \$701.69$
2. **Calculate the total amount repaid**
$\text{Total repaid} = 60 \times \$701.69 = \$42\,101.40$
3. **Calculate the total interest**
$\text{Interest} = \$42\,101.40 - \$34\,600 = \$7501.40$
